subject: Art & Design
title: Modular and Prefab: Factory-Made Buildings
description: A 60-second lesson on Modular and Prefab: Factory-Made Buildings.

hook.text: A Chinese company 3D-printed 10 houses in 24 hours. Each cost under $5,000. The construction industry noticed.

buildup.text: Prefab construction assembles building sections in factories, then ships and connects them on site.

discovery.text: Factory conditions mean higher quality, less waste, faster construction, and fewer weather delays.

twist.text: Prefab has a stigma: cheap, temporary, ugly. Modern modular architects are proving those stereotypes obsolete.

climax.text: 3D-printed concrete, cross-laminated timber, and robotics may make traditional construction the exception, not the rule.

punchline.text: The future of building might not happen at the building site.

quiz.question: What is the main advantage of prefab/modular construction?
options: Higher quality, less waste, and faster construction in controlled factory conditions
The buildings last longer than traditional ones

details.summary: Modern prefabrication manufactures building modules in factories and assembles them on-site in days. Factory conditions improve quality, reduce waste by up to 80%, and eliminate weather delays.
details.whyItMatters: Traditional construction is one of the least productive industries. Prefabrication brings manufacturing efficiency to building, producing higher quality at lower cost while dramatically reducing construction time and waste.
takeaways: Factory-built modules are assembled on-site in days
Waste is reduced by up to 80% versus conventional methods
Multi-story buildings can be assembled from stacked modules

faq.question: Are prefab buildings lower quality than traditional?
faq.answer: Often higher quality. Factory conditions enable precise quality control, consistent material handling, and inspection at every stage. Joints and finishes are typically more accurate than field-built equivalents. Negative reputation comes from early, lower-quality prefab eras.

faq.question: Can prefab create architecturally interesting buildings?
faq.answer: Absolutely. Habitat 67 in Montreal showed in 1967 that prefab modules could create sculptural, visually striking architecture. Modern prefab firms produce custom-designed modules that are indistinguishable from site-built construction in their finished appearance.
